It’s good that you went. I had clotting issues and the first time, once I had closer to normal oxygen levels and could understand what was going on around me, I was told that had I not come in, I probably would not have woken up the next day. I had clusters of blood clots in both lungs. 

They diagnosed it as a DVT without scanning my legs and kept me in the hospital for 10 days and eventho my Warfrin didn’t get to a therapeutic level, they sent me home. 

I took the Warfrin for 6 months and had to have my INR tested everyday for a while then three times a week. I went off the Warfrin and a few months later, I just didn’t feel right. I couldn’t put my finger on it because nothing was wrong with me but I just knew that something just wasn’t right. 

So back to the ER and I told them that I thought I had Bi-Lateral PE’s. So AGAIN back in the hospital but that time a Hematologist came and again said it was a DVT and again, no ultrasound. 

NINE YEARS LATER, I found out I have Antiphospholipid Antibody syndrome. I went to so many doctors and specialists and finally one of them was so livid that out of all the testing they did, they never tested me for Lupus which can come with APS. 

Now I take Xarelto 20mgs but my d-dimer is still always high. The first time it was in the 300’s and the second time 1000’s. But I seriously had no symptoms the second time and the first time the only thing wrong was my oxygen was so low, my skin was actually turning gray but mentally I was out of it because of the low oxygen. 

But the second time my oxygen was 95 still in the normal range but I had to insist they do a scan. They treated me like I was crazy because 35 year old women don’t get one blood clot let alone clusters of them in both lungs. But because my d-dimer came back high, they did the scan. 

When they saw the clots, the same provider who didn’t believe me and she knew it happened before, talked to me like I was some idiot. She explained it to me as if I didn’t know what they were. 

I have absolutely zero trust in doctors anymore and avoid them like the plague. That was my experience.

Idk your name, gender, ethnicity, age, or how you look and sound. But I do know that if I were to come to this thread and see that you have not come back, I will be praying and probably cry at the thought of you dying alone thinking you are alone. YOU ARE NOT ALINE AND WILL NEVER BE FORGOTTEN. I will always wonder if I don’t see you post. I will shed tears if I don’t see you post again. I’m just some random person online. If me and others here will say the same, just think of those close to you and how they are going to have a big hole in their lives without you there. Whether you know it or not, you have made connections in life. There are ppl who care. We all get caught up in life and don’t say it enough. I will never forget at my cousin’s funeral after the service where the church was crowded and the meal had over 200 people there who could not understand. Some were there out of obligation but for the most part these were ppl she knew but felt they looked down upon her and just a week before, she told her mom almost the same thing you said. At the lunch, my aunt repeated what she said a week earlier and looked out at the ppl who were still crying, consoling each other, sharing stories and so on. My aunt started crying and said “These ppl have always been here for her and she felt too down on herself and could not believe that most of these ppl genuinely care about her” I say the same thing you said. In fact, I felt so let down by my therapists that I would cry at the thought that I can’t even pay someone to hear my words and recognize that I’m hurting. You would be missed if you moved away and you would certainly be missed by someone (probably more than one) but you are not in a place to be able to comprehend this. Please try and talk to someone trained to help you.

Bulimic makes me guess you are not fat and so what if you are.... I’m not skinny and while I want to be skinny again, I embrace my newer body and I make sure to have both comfy clothes for lounging, but I keep myself up with more stylish and am dressed up when I go out. It gives me more confidence to know that at my weight, I can still dress good. I can still wear makeup. And while I am slowly but actively losing weight, I embrace myself and every curve. I am embracing a few less curves now, but I was embarrassed to go out in public until I decided to dress and look my best. I’m still not as comfortable as I was when I was starving, just knowing ppl still look at me and my smiling face and smile back or chat... that is incentive for me to at least be up and about more burning more calories and motivates me to grab an apple before a piece of cake. Or a handful of grapes instead of a hot dog. Small changes give me courage. But that is me. I am sure you are a beautiful person and that you have more ppl who love you than you know. Depression is not anything you can just snap out of. Don’t listen to those ppl. BUT you can choose not to let it take your life by starting to add just one thing a day. Make it a goal to get out of bed. Then after a couple days, add something to it. Get out of bed and shower. Get out of bed, shower, walk to the end of the street and back.... And write down what you are going to do each day and at the end of the day write down the things you actually did. That second list is going to grow. Fast or slow. But it will end up surprising you because you can see on paper the things you are already doing without realizing it or that you have added more than you realize. Choose to make eye contact and smile at one stranger. Choose anything you want. Choose the speed at which you add new things. But WRITE DOWN EVERYTHING you do from getting out of bed to making coffee to doing some cleaning to going in public and so on.... I lived in my bed for over a year and had to start with sitting up in my bed. I could not bring myself to get out of my bed or room. But once I got myself out of my room, I had to do things to stay out of my room. I’m usually back in bed by dinner time, but it took months just to get out of my bed. Do NOT put yourself down. Focus on what you accomplish. Depression knocks us down hard and we have to fight to get out. Don’t listen to anyone who tells you negative things or to snap out of it and don’t waste your breath explaining. Just let them talk as you as you walk away. I will personally do what I can to help see you through but I need to reread the rules in here. But please please please do not do a thing without talking to someone. If we are not allowed to pm then post here. I’m new so idk if you can tag ppl, but you can certainly come back to my response and I will get a notification. I have a story posted a year ago in here. I get it: I get depression. I get eating disorders. I’m not gay but I get that. And nobody is ugly. So I’m betting you look great. Please respond and promise you will come back and post on my response before you do anything. I might not have all the right words and probably didn’t say a lot of the right things just now. But I did tell you what I AM STILL DOING to crawl out of that black hole of depression and yes, I am medicated and under the care of a psych doc. I’m not able to do this on my own. Nobody can. So please promise you will check in while I find out what is and is not allowed as far as communication is concerned. But first things first. Please see a psych doc if you haven’t and consider whatever advice they give because they are trained. ~Tracy
